text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Repairing mildrew damage to houses in Finland may cost up to 34 billion markka -- almost the same amount as the bill for bank support.
- Finnish information technology firms suffer from lack of competent personnel which hinders growth in the sector, industry says.
- Judging from all warnings ahead of Christmas, the festivities turn increasingly dangerous from year to year, but statistics disagree.
- Russian Autovaz says plans plant in Vyborg to assemble Opel Astra cars.
- Finland can now tap bond markets at better terms than Sweden, and considers issuing a benchmark maturing in 2008, top finance ministry official says.
- Asko's textiles division consisting of Suomen Trikoo and Finlayson is profitable and paper says would be a candidate for the group to sell, but CEO says no talks ongoing.
- A majority of Finns do not expect unemployment to fall with the government's current methods, survey shows.
- Thirty patients at Helsinki's Meilahti hospital have been infected with mutated bacteria which are resistant to anti-biotics and two wards with some 70 patients have been isolated.
